anatomicalReference: In the rear view, the potion-pouch side is anatomical right (viewer right). Identify each boot from its thigh/calf connection, not from its horizontal pixel position alone.

phases.requirement: Contact/support A: one identifiable planted leg and the opposite visibly trailing or lifted boot/heel. Both boots are readable.
Passing A: the swing leg passes the planted support leg. The two ankles/boots remain distinguishable; this is not the same central boot merely shifted vertically.
Opposite contact/support B: planted and trailing/lifted anatomical legs exchange roles relative to phase 1. The opposite heel is visibly presented.
Opposite passing B: the other anatomical leg passes the new support leg. Roles differ from phase 2, with contralateral arm motion.

checks: Inspect all four stills at 64px and 120px, then a 3fps slow loop and the runtime movement loop.
Two boots must remain separable by contour or shading at gameplay scale; robe coverage must not hide all evidence of alternation.
Phase 1 versus 3 and phase 2 versus 4 must exchange anatomical support/swing roles, rather than repeat one-leg hopping.
The planted-foot baseline and body center must remain stable; apparent sliding is assessed against the moving ground in the runtime recording.
The pouch stays on anatomical right. No frame mirroring is permitted.
UP-only historical proof preserves all other visible RGB and alpha. Subsequent RIGHT-only proof preserves new UP, DOWN, LEFT and ATTACK; transparent RGB normalization is reported separately.
Alpha bounds, unique frame hashes, and cycling frame indexes alone are not evidence of anatomical leg alternation.
findings: At 64px and 120px the rear boots remain distinguishable. Pouch-side right sole is exposed in phase 2; left sole is exposed in phase 4.
Rear phase 1 trails the right boot and phase 3 trails the left boot; the old single central boot pattern is replaced.
Right-facing hat brooch is absent in all four frames. Front and left-facing hat brooches remain.
Automated frame progression is runtime evidence, not independent proof of anatomical gait.
